# grafana_assistant_automation (Resource)

Manages a Grafana Assistant Automation: a saved Assistant prompt that runs on
demand or on a cron schedule. Each run creates its own Assistant conversation.

Automations are a Grafana Cloud-only feature and require the Grafana Assistant app.

execution_mode selects the identity used for runs. The default user mode uses the creator's
Grafana permissions. service_account mode requires tenant scope and organization Admin
permission to configure. Authenticating Terraform with a service-account token does not
automatically select service_account execution. Runtime memory and run history remain backend-owned.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "grafana_assistant_automation" "daily_incident_report" {
  name        = "Daily ecommerce incident report"
  description = "Every morning, summarize the alerts that fired for the ecommerce app."

  prompt = <<-EOT
    Produce a daily report on the incidents for the main alerts that fired in
    the last 24 hours for the ecommerce app in the ecommerce-prod namespace.

    For each alert: how long it fired, which services were affected, and
    whether it correlates with a deploy. Close with the single most important
    thing to look at today.
  EOT

  # Shared with everybody in the org, rather than private to the creator.
  scope   = "tenant"
  enabled = true

  # Default: runs use the creator's permissions.
  # service_account requires tenant scope and organization Admin permission.
  execution_mode = "user"
  labels = {
    application = "ecommerce"
    managed_by  = "terraform"
  }

  # Multiple expressions can be separated by semicolons.
  # Combined firings must be at least 15 minutes apart.
  schedule_cron     = "0 9 * * *"
  schedule_timezone = "Europe/Paris"
  # Optional, if the backend enables bounded schedules. Omit to clear.
  # schedule_ends_at = "2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"

  notifications {
    slack {
      enabled   = true
      notify_on = ["completed", "failed"]

      target {
        type       = "channel"
        channel_id = "C0123456789"
      }
    }
  }
}

# Event-only automation. Replace the watcher UUID with an existing Watcher.
# The backend must enable Watcher-to-Automation triggers. No events run while disabled.
resource "grafana_assistant_automation" "on_critical_finding" {
  name           = "Investigate critical Watcher findings"
  prompt         = "Investigate the critical finding supplied by the Watcher event."
  scope          = "tenant"
  execution_mode = "service_account"
  enabled        = false

  # Trigger keys are stable UUIDs. Do not call uuid() here: it changes each plan.
  # Keep the key when editing a trigger; remove its entry to unsubscribe.
  triggers = {
    "c971a626-703b-4472-8eb0-e92aaf705af9" = {
      type = "watcher_finding"
      config = jsonencode({
        watcherId = "52fcc709-4ab5-45c8-8f79-a1c1d6abef17"
      })
    }
  }
}

# A manual-only automation needs neither schedule nor timezone.
resource "grafana_assistant_automation" "manual_report" {
  name    = "On-demand incident report"
  prompt  = "Summarize the incidents from the past 24 hours."
  enabled = false
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-friendly automation name.
- `prompt` (String) The prompt sent to Assistant on each run. Prefix with `/<skill-name>` to start from a skill.

### Optional

- `context_items` (String) Context items attached to the prompt, as a JSON array string.
- `description` (String) Optional description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the automation runs on its schedule. Disabled automations can still be run manually.
- `execution_mode` (String) Run identity: user (default) or service_account. service_account requires scope = tenant and Grafana organization Admin permission, including updates to an existing service-account automation.
- `labels` (Map of String) Operator labels. Omit or use an empty map to remove managed labels.
- `notifications` (Block, Optional) Where to send the result of each run. Webhook notifications are not supported by this resource because their URL and credentials are write-only secure settings the API never returns. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--notifications))
- `schedule_cron` (String) Standard 5-field cron expression, or multiple expressions separated by semicolons. For example `0 9 * * 1-5; 0 10 * * 0`. Omit for a manual-only automation. Combined firings must be at least 15 minutes apart.
- `schedule_ends_at` (String) Inclusive schedule deadline in RFC3339 format with second precision. Requires schedule_cron and backend support for bounded schedules. Omit to remove the deadline. New or changed deadlines must be in the future.
- `schedule_timezone` (String) IANA timezone the schedule is interpreted in, for example `Europe/Paris`. Defaults to UTC when schedule_cron is set; absent for manual-only automations.
- `scope` (String) Visibility. `user` keeps the automation private to its creator; `tenant` shares it with everybody in the org.
- `triggers` (Map of Object) Event triggers keyed by stable, lowercase UUIDs. Each value requires type (backend trigger type) and config (a JSON object string, normally jsonencode). Keep UUIDs unchanged when editing. Omit or use an empty map to remove all triggers. GitHub and Watcher triggers require service_account execution; Slack triggers run as the mapped event author. Backend defaults and equivalent JSON formatting do not cause drift. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--triggers))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The UUID of the resource.
- `next_run_at` (String) When the automation is next scheduled to fire.

<a id="nestedblock--notifications"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notifications`

Optional:

- `email` (Block, Optional) Email delivery. Email notifications must be enabled for the stack. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--notifications--email))
- `slack` (Block, Optional) Slack delivery. Requires the Slack workspace to already be connected to the stack, which is a one-time manual step in Assistant settings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--notifications--slack))

<a id="nestedblock--notifications--email"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notifications.email`

Optional:

- `addresses` (List of String) Recipient email addresses, up to 25.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether email notifications are sent.
- `notify_on` (List of String) Run outcomes that trigger a notification. Any of `completed`, `failed`, `needs_approval`.


<a id="nestedblock--notifications--slack"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notifications.slack`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether Slack notifications are sent.
- `notify_on` (List of String) Run outcomes that trigger a notification. Any of `completed`, `failed`, `needs_approval`.
- `target` (Block, Optional) Where the notification is posted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--notifications--slack--target))

<a id="nestedblock--notifications--slack--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notifications.slack.target`

Optional:

- `channel_id` (String) Slack channel ID. Required for a `channel` target.
- `team_id` (String) Slack workspace (team) ID. Omit to let Assistant resolve it; automatically resolved IDs are not managed unless configured.
- `type` (String) Target type. One of `channel` or `dm`. Required when a `target` block is present.
- `user_id` (String) Slack user ID for a `dm` target. Omit to use the creator’s verified Slack mapping.




<a id="nestedatt--triggers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `triggers`

Optional:

- `config` (String)
- `type` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import grafana_assistant_automation.name "{{ id }}"
```
